v.q: What separates continuous delivery from continuous deployment?
o: A person decides when to release
v.w: In delivery every change is ready to release and a person presses the button. In deployment every passing change goes live automatically.

v.q: Which practice is the core of continuous integration?
o: Merging small changes into main often
Keeping one long branch per feature
Running tests only before a release
v.w: CI is frequent integration, each merge built and tested automatically. A server alone does not make a team do CI.

v.q: Which order of pipeline stages is best?
o: Fast checks first, slow ones later
v.w: Fail fast: cheap checks like compile and unit tests run first, so the author learns about a problem in minutes.

v.q: Which step does NOT belong before the artifact is published?
v.w: Publishing stores the tested artifact. Production comes after it, using the same artifact.

v.q: Why build the artifact once and promote it?
o: Production runs exactly what was tested
Builds for each environment are faster
It removes the need for a registry
v.w: Rebuilding per environment can pick up different dependencies, so production may run something never tested.

v.q: Which image tag is best for a production deployment?
o: The commit hash or a version
A branch name such as main
v.w: An immutable tag shows what runs and what to roll back to. A moving tag like latest does not.

v.q: What is the main problem with a long-lived feature branch?
o: The final merge is large and risky
It cannot be reviewed at all
v.w: The branch drifts from main, so conflicts pile up and the combination is untested until the end.

v.q: Which model suits continuous delivery best?
o: One branch per developer for months
v.w: Trunk-based development keeps integration cheap and main releasable. Gitflow delays integration.

v.q: What does a feature flag let a team do?
v.w: The code is merged and deployed with the flag off, and the feature is released later by switching the flag on.

v.q: Which is a cost of feature flags?
o: Extra code paths to test and remove
v.w: Flags add paths to test and become clutter if they are not removed once the feature is fully released.

v.q: When does a quality gate have value?
o: It is optional for urgent changes
v.w: A gate must stop the change. A report that nobody has to act on is just noise.

v.q: Which check is a dependency scan for?
v.w: Software composition analysis, such as Dependency-Check, Snyk or Trivy, finds libraries with known CVEs.

v.q: Why can rolling back sometimes be impossible?
o: The old image was deleted by Git
v.w: If data was already migrated, the old version may not work with it. Then you roll forward with a fix.

v.w: The same artifact runs everywhere and settings come from variables, a config server or Secrets.

v.q: Which is one of the four DORA metrics?
v.w: The four are deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate and time to restore.

v.q: How does a bank usually keep four-eyes control in a pipeline?
o: Required reviewers and a gated approval
v.w: Branch protection and an approval stage ensure that someone other than the author signs off, and the pipeline keeps the evidence.
